title: More People Are Using Their Library Cards
summary: When money is tight, many people turn to the library. Izzy Rivera lives in Topeka, Kansas. She reads at least one book every week. But she is saving money for law school, so she cannot always buy new books. "Say I'm buying a few a month," she said. "It just isn't realistic." So Rivera borrows books from her library. Last month she bought 15 used books for about $20 at a library book sale. "It's somewhere I can go where I'm not expected to spend money," she said. A survey found that 44% of Americans had trouble paying for a basic need last year, and 70% cut back on extras like streaming. Big libraries across the country say more people are joining, borrowing books and coming to events. In Los Angeles, use of the library's makerspace grew 37%. Libraries lend more than books. Many lend Wi-Fi hotspots, cooking tools, bird-watching kits and camping gear. But library money is under pressure: last year, the Trump administration tried to cut funding, but 21 states went to court and the money was saved.
why_it_matters: Your library card can get you books, movies and tools for free, which helps when money is tight at home.
